questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether nuclear power helps or harms the climate
Why oil and gas prices rise in the winter
How the Chernobyl power station was built
Why Germany uses so much wind and solar power
questions.why: Sam says they'll ask whether, when it comes to the climate, nuclear is a friend or foe.

questions.q: What do people who prefer nuclear energy argue?
options: It is much cheaper than oil and natural gas
It can be built quickly in any country
It's clean and more reliable than renewables
It creates more jobs than any other energy
questions.why: Neil says they argue it's clean, green and more reliable than renewables.

questions.q: Why do questions about nuclear safety remain?
options: Many power stations have no workers
Because of disasters like Chernobyl
Nuclear stations are often in big cities
Scientists have never tested them
questions.why: Neil says after nuclear disasters like Chernobyl and Fukushima, questions about its safety remain.

questions.q: What does Mirjam Vossen remember about the Chernobyl disaster?
options: She was working as a journalist in Ukraine
The media hardly reported on it at all
People in Europe were not very worried
Everyone was scared of the radioactive clouds
questions.why: She has vivid memories of how scary it was and how frightened everyone was of the radioactive clouds.

questions.q: What does Mirjam believe about people's views on nuclear safety today?
options: They are correct and should not change
They are based on modern power stations
They are out of date
They are too positive about nuclear power
questions.why: She believes these ingrained perceptions are out-of-date, as such accidents couldn't happen in modern stations.

questions.q: What advantage does nuclear have over renewables, according to Neil?
options: It gives a steady supply of power
It produces no waste at all
It needs no water to cool down
It is safer than wind power
questions.why: Neil says nuclear gives a steady supply, unlike renewables when the wind doesn't blow or the Sun doesn't shine.

questions.q: Why does Paul Dorfman think nuclear power has no future?
options: Because it produces too much carbon
Because the public will never trust it
Because there isn't enough uranium left
Rising seas threaten stations near water
questions.why: Stations are located near seas or lakes for cooling, and he thinks rising sea levels will end nuclear as an option.

questions.q: What does Paul Dorfman think should be done with the money?
options: It should be used to build new nuclear stations
It should make renewables more reliable
It should be spent on oil and natural gas
It should protect stations from the sea
questions.why: Sam says he thinks money for nuclear upgrades would be better spent making clean renewables more reliable.
